Changed regions include col0 rows5,6! They're on the border yet changed. And row0 cols3 etc changed even though top border. So border-touching alone doesn't keep. What distinguishes? Perhaps the 9s act as walls and the region containing... all 1-cells change to 3 EXCEPT those in a particular region? The "X" map shows kept = left top L-shape + right top corner + bottom-right blob. Changed everywhere else. These three kept blobs touch the border too. Hmm — maybe kept = 1-cells not adjacent (4-dir or 8-dir?) to any 9? Maybe it's about enclosed regions: kept = components of 1 that do not touch a 9 within distance...? Or the rule: each 9 expands? Contradiction unless connectivity is limited.

Bottom-right kept blob (7,8)-(7,14): surrounded by 9? row7 has 9s at 0,4,5,7. Row 6 above has 9 at 11. Left of blob: (7,7)=9, (6,8..10)=1. Top: (6,8..10)=1. Not fully walled.

Alternative view: count of 9s per row/column? Maybe the transformation colors a cell 3 if number of 9s in its row ≥ something? Rows with ≥5 nines? Row7 has 4 nines, all its 1s changed except 8-14. Row0 has 4 nines, cols 3,5,6,8,9 changed, 0,1,11-14 stayed.

With 4-neighborhood, 9s block movement; each blob is a closed pocket of 1s cut off from other 1s by 9s — that's exactly a flood fill of 1s where 9s block. Kept = components of 1s NOT touching border? No—blob touches border (top-left at col0, top edge). Unless blocked pockets = pockets bounded entirely by 9s (no need to touch border)... Top-left L touches left/top border, so "bounded by 9s" fails... unless we consider the grid border as wall too! Then all three blobs are pockets enclosed by borders+9s, and the big region is also enclosed by borders+9s. Both enclosed. Doesn't separate.

OK different idea: maybe cells change to 3 if they have a 9-neighboring in BOTH... no.

Let me look at exact boundary: which 9-adjacency does a kept cell lack vs changed? Compute for each kept cell the nearest 9 and compare with changed.
